analysis.title: Morning Report 29 October 2026
key_insights: The Fed held rates at the October meeting with two dissents (Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack), both preferring a 25bp hike. Westpac reads the dissents, Chair Warsh's note that consumer inflation has been above target for 6 years, and his comment that accumulating information will help determine the stance as pointing to another 25bp hike in December.

Chair Warsh announced a structural change from 2027: one fall meeting will focus on monetary policy strategy rather than the current policy stance. He intends 2 of the 8 meetings in 2028 to have this strategy focus.

The US 2-year yield rose initially after the Fed hold, then closed 3bps lower as Warsh said the Fed would assess incoming information and not prejudge December. The 10-year yield rose 3bps as markets focused on his comments on tighter financial conditions. Futures still put the chance of a December hike at 85%.
The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 25bps, its first hike in three years, as expected. It projects growth of 1% in 2026 and 2% in 2027 and 2028, somewhat stronger than the July Report.
The RBNZ held the OCR at 2.75% in a surprise decision. The committee voted 4:3 against a 25bp hike, and a hike remains largely priced by year-end.

Australian September CPI was firm at +0.8% m/m and 4.3% y/y. The monthly trimmed mean was 0.3% m/m and 3.6% y/y, within 3.5-3.6% for five consecutive months. The quarterly trimmed mean was 1.0% q/q and 3.7% y/y. Australian 3-year and 10-year yields rose 6bps, and swaps price an 85% chance of an RBA hike next week, with a hike fully priced by year-end.

Oil rose on reports the US could resume attacks on Iran after the midterms, and pared gains after Iran's Foreign Minister said the country continues to give diplomacy a chance. Brent closed 1.0% higher at US$115.0/bbl and WTI gained 2.7% to US$102.6/bbl.

US equities closed higher after the Fed decision (S&P 500 and Nasdaq +0.3%, Dow +0.2%). Asian equities rallied on strong earnings reviving AI optimism, with the Kospi up 6.6% to a two-week high and the Nikkei up 1.1%.

UK Chancellor Healey's Budget was modest, with £4.1bn of cost-of-living relief and a pledge to lift defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030. The tax increase on lenders was less severe than feared, and the 10-year gilt yield fell 3bps.
The USD index fell 0.2%. AUD rose 0.5% against the USD and 1.4% against the NZD, touching a 13-year high against the NZD. EUR and GBP also gained against the dollar.

Key US data due today (AEDT times): Q3 GDP advance (consensus 3.2% vs 2.2% prior), September PCE deflator (0.5% vs 0.3%), core PCE (0.3% vs 0.2%), personal spending (0.6%), initial jobless claims (198k), and the ECB policy decision (2.6% expected, unchanged).
